bottom_line: In chronic heart failure, high-dose vs low-dose lisinopril did not significantly reduce all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 0.92 [0.82–1.03]).
implications: These data show no statistically significant difference in all-cause mortality between high-dose and low-dose lisinopril (hazard ratio 0.92 [0.82–1.03], P=0.128), while supporting a lower risk of death or hospitalization for any reason with high-dose (0.88 [0.82–0.96], P=0.002) and fewer heart-failure hospitalizations (1576 vs 1199; 24% reduction; P=0.002). The findings also indicate more frequent dizziness (19% vs 12%) and hyperkalemia (6% vs 4%) with high-dose in this trial.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind comparison of low-dose vs high-dose lisinopril in chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned 3164 patients with New York Heart Association class II to IV heart failure and an ejection fraction #30% to double-blind treatment with either low doses (2.5 to 5.0 mg daily, n51596) or high doses (32.5 to 35 mg daily, n51568)

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was all-cause mortality; follow-up ranged 39 to 58 months (median 45.7).
major_points.quote: The primary end point was all-cause mortality

major_points.text: All-cause mortality result was not statistically significant.
High-dose reduced the prioritized combined endpoint of death or hospitalization for any reason.
High-dose strategy produced fewer total hospitalizations for heart failure.

criticisms.text: The primary endpoint (all-cause mortality) did not show a significant difference between groups.
criticisms.quote: Nevertheless, the present study did not observe a signifi- cant difference between the 2 treatment groups in the risk of death, the primary end point of the study.

criticisms.text: The study cannot predict what would have been observed versus placebo or versus intermediate doses.
criticisms.quote: our results cannot predict what we might have observed if low doses of ACE inhibitors had been compared with placebo or if high doses of ACE inhibitors had been compared with intermediate doses of these drugs.

criticisms.text: Observed mortality rate was lower than expected and many patients were not maintained on assigned study medications.
criticisms.quote: Yet the observed annual mortality rate in the trial was only 15%, and many patients were not maintained on their assigned study medications.

criticisms.text: Protocol added the combined risk of all-cause mortality and hospitalization for any reason during the trial as a secondary endpoint.
